problem: LLM-based control of quadruped robots needs more compute than the robot's onboard hardware provides, and existing solutions rely on onboard high-end GPUs or static servers. Conventional control interfaces also require expert knowledge.
motivation: Non-expert users need to command legged robots in natural language, but lightweight, low-cost platforms cannot run LLMs locally. The paper offloads LLM inference to an external host or cloud API while keeping local ROS navigation on the robot.
key_idea: Offload LLM planning (Gemini via a prompted JSON motion planner) to a development host or cloud, and ground the resulting JSON action list into ROS move_base goto commands over a pre-built semantic waypoint map on a Jueying Lite 3 quadruped.
insight: A carefully constrained prompt (action primitives, waypoint constraints, few-shot examples) gives reliable JSON plans. The paper reports no semantic errors in the generated JSON, so the few failures come from local navigation rather than from the LLM. There is no ablation, baseline or comparison, so the evidence is only the four-scenario success rates.
method: Distributed architecture: user device, development host (LLM requests, Flask web server), perception host (Jetson Xavier NX; localization, planning), motion host (actuators, LiDAR/IMU/odometry), and a Wi-Fi access point
Mapping and semantic waypoints: HDL-Localization 3D LiDAR SLAM map of the Tower 2 9th floor at ITS; POIs (labs, pantry, elevators, restrooms) each with global x,y,z coordinates

LLM prompt design: Vertex AI Gemini system prompt enforcing strict JSON output with an 'actions' array (goto, wait, etc.), action primitives, constraints against hallucinated waypoints, and few-shot examples
Plan grounding: the JSON is parsed by the development host and published to the ROS move_base topic, so the navigation stack executes point-to-point global planning
Web interface: a Flask web app on the robot accepts Indonesian natural-language instructions from a phone or computer and calls the cloud LLM API

setting.backbone: Vertex AI Gemini (frozen, prompted; exact version not stated)
setting.observation: LiDAR, IMU and odometry on a pre-built 3D SLAM map
setting.action_space: LLM emits semantic waypoint goto commands, executed via ROS move_base global planning
setting.privileged: pre-built SLAM map and manually defined semantic waypoint coordinates; manual localization in RViz

numbers_note: Results are on a custom real-world indoor test (four scenarios, SR and duration only), not on any standard benchmark, so no benchmark entries are listed. Table values: Single-room 100% SR / 45.26 s / 15 trials; Multi-room short 96% / 68.27 s / 25; Multi-room long 90% / 89.71 s / 20; Cross-zone 100% / 130.98 s / 20. The text says the cross-zone SR is 100% while the abstract says an aggregate above 90%.
results: The system achieves 90-100% success across the four custom scenarios (single-room 100%, short multi-room 96%, long multi-room 90%, cross-zone 100%). Task time grows with the number of waypoints, from 45 s to 131 s. There are no baselines.
limitations: Small trial counts (15-25 per scenario) on a single floor, with no baselines or ablations
Depends on a pre-built map and manually defined waypoints, and on a cloud LLM/network connection
Failures were in local navigation during room transitions; there is no visual grounding or memory (RAG and VLM are left as future work)
